cards.ja: 緊急通報のオペレーター
助けてください、緊急事態です！

cards.en: Can you call an ambulance, please?
cards.ja: 救急車を呼んでいただけますか。
cards.glossEn: Can you call an ambulance, please?

cards.en: A man fell at the next table.
cards.ja: 隣のテーブルで男性が倒れました。
cards.glossEn: A man fell at the next table.

cards.en: What is the exact address of the café?
cards.ja: このカフェの正確な住所は何ですか。
cards.glossEn: What is the exact address of the café?

cards.en: I don't know if he is breathing well.
cards.ja: 彼がちゃんと呼吸しているか分かりません。
cards.glossEn: I don't know if he is breathing well.

cards.en: We are on the corner of Juárez and Madero.
cards.ja: フアレス通りとマデロ通りの交差点の角にいます。
cards.glossEn: We are on the corner of Juárez and Madero.

reader.en: I am having breakfast in a café when the customer at the next table falls to the floor.
reader.ja: カフェで朝食をとっていると、隣のテーブルの客が床に倒れます。
reader.glossEn: I am having breakfast in a café when the customer at the next table falls to the floor.

reader.en: I stand up and say to the waiter: Help, please, it's an emergency!
reader.ja: 私は立ち上がり、ウェイターに「助けてください、緊急事態です！」と言います。
reader.glossEn: I stand up and say to the waiter: Help, please, it's an emergency!

reader.en: The manager comes quickly and I ask him: Can you call an ambulance, please?
reader.ja: 責任者がすぐに来たので、私は彼に「救急車を呼んでいただけますか」と尋ねます。
reader.glossEn: The manager comes quickly and I ask him: Can you call an ambulance, please?

reader.en: He dials the emergency number and the operator asks him for the address.
reader.ja: 彼が緊急通報番号に電話をかけると、オペレーターが住所を尋ねます。
reader.glossEn: He dials the emergency number and the operator asks him for the address.

reader.en: The manager answers: We are on the corner of Juárez and Madero, next to the bank.
reader.ja: 責任者は「フアレス通りとマデロ通りの交差点の角、銀行の隣です」と答えます。
reader.glossEn: The manager answers: We are on the corner of Juárez and Madero, next to the bank.

reader.en: Then the operator wants to know what happened, because that information helps the paramedics.
reader.ja: その後、オペレーターは何が起きたか知りたがります。その情報が救急隊員の役に立つからです。
reader.glossEn: Then the operator wants to know what happened, because that information helps the paramedics.

reader.en: I explain to her: A man fell at the next table and he isn't answering.
reader.ja: 私は「隣のテーブルで男性が倒れ、返事がありません」と説明します。
reader.glossEn: I explain to her: A man fell at the next table and he isn't answering.

reader.en: I also tell her: I don't know if he is breathing well.
reader.ja: さらに「彼がちゃんと呼吸しているか分かりません」と伝えます。
reader.glossEn: I also tell her: I don't know if he is breathing well.

reader.en: Then I wait at the door to show the table to the paramedics when they arrive.
reader.ja: そして、救急隊員が到着したらそのテーブルへ案内できるよう、入口で待ちます。
reader.glossEn: Then I wait at the door to show the table to the paramedics when they arrive.

issues: Qualified Japanese and clinical reviewers must choose whether 倒れる accurately expresses source se cayó / fell or whether a fall-specific verb better preserves the observed event without implying a diagnosis.
ウェイター and 責任者 are source roles; verify natural Japanese café role wording and when the source masculine labels are relevant.
緊急通報番号 and 緊急通報のオペレーター retain generic source terms; locale-specific emergency number and dispatcher labels require qualified review before a learner prompt.
Juárez and Madero street names are transliterated as フアレス and マデロ; confirm spelling and address rendering with a qualified locale reviewer.
「ちゃんと呼吸しているか分かりません」 is an observation, not a diagnosis; verify wording against source no sé si respira bien and clinical usage.
Source Card 15 says a man fell; Reader 7 adds that he does not answer. Confirm the card/Reader distinction and dictionary senses before any learner scoring or speaking.
The old archived dialogue gives local-service advice and a location-finding step absent from current source; review retired positions without carrying those into new activity answers.
